chunk_a.text_snippet:
Title: ICE agents reveal daily arrest quotas and surveillance app in rare court testimony
Date: 2026-03-13

Content: JB said he did not know how Elite “leads” were generated, saying the app “pulls from all kinds of sources”. JB acknowledged information generated by Elite could be inaccurate: “The app could say 100%, and it’s wrong. The person doesn’t live there. And so it’s not accurate. It’s a tool that we use that gives you probability, but there’s … no such thing as 100%.” Officers have to do “checks” on the intelligence, he said. At the apartment complex, officers ran license plates of vehicles and became interested in the van when a search in their databases suggested the van’s owner was possibly an immigrant in the US without authorization. JB said the team decided to follow the van once it departed, even though officers didn’t confirm whether the driver of the van was, in fact, the registered owner of the vehicle.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: ICE arrested an Oregon shop owner who had her green card in her pocket: ‘They didn’t care’
Date: 2026-03-06

Content: Instead, ICE was consistently violating people’s due-process rights, often stopping them based on their skin color, with no justification. The suit exposed details of how ICE had targeted people without warrants, with officers testifying about the Department of Homeland Security’s “Operation Black Rose”, which launched in Portland last fall and, according to DHS, led to more than 1,200 arrests through mid-December. One ICE officer testified that Black Rose teams of roughly nine to 12 officers were told to target eight arrests per day, with plaintiff’s attorneys estimating this amounted to a daily quota of 50 arrests across Oregon. The officer also revealed agents chose locations with help from a DHS app called “Elite”, which identified target areas where there might be multiple people with some “nexus” to immigration (including documented immigrants without violations).

t_bridge: ICE operational practices and target identification
Validity and limitations of intelligence-driven enforcement

initial_question.rag_input: How did the Elite app's target identification method contribute to the operational pressure of daily arrest quotas reported by ICE officers in March 2026?
initial_question.question: How did the Elite app's target identification method contribute to the operational pressure of daily arrest quotas reported by ICE officers in March 2026?
initial_question.answer: In March 2026, ICE officers revealed that the 'Elite' app identified areas with potential immigration 'nexus' to assist in meeting the operational mandate of 'Operation Black Rose,' which required teams of 9 to 12 officers to achieve eight arrests per day. However, agents also testified that this intelligence-driven tool is prone to inaccuracy, as it provides probability rather than confirmation, forcing officers to conduct their own checks while under pressure to meet these daily arrest quotas.
initial_question.bridging_topic: Relationship between Elite app targeting and ICE daily arrest quotas.
